conventions.convention: The pairing is linear in its first argument. Rank-one operators are T(u,v)x = ⟨x,v⟩u, with trace ⟨u,v⟩.
A declared ideal sharp measurement consists of finitely or countably many mutually orthogonal bounded orthogonal projections whose sum is I strongly.
Conditional states are defined only for outcomes of strictly positive probability. Discarded-outcome states sum unnormalized branches in trace norm; zero-probability branches vanish.
A Kraus instrument includes its update rule, not merely its effects. Its total Kraus index set is finite or countable, normalization is strong, and grouped branch updates converge in trace norm.

Repeatability concerns immediate repetition of the same declared instrument, for every input state and every positive-probability outcome. The countable repeatability theorem uses one Kraus operator per outcome.
The selective and nonselective mathematical lemmas assume Countable Choice. The general spectral-eigenspace and continuous-functional-calculus dilation arguments additionally assume Choice.
All physical conclusions concern declared models. No apparatus realization, unique recorded outcome, observed count or empirical agreement follows from these computations.

load_bearing.statement: Under the adopted P1, P2 and P3, declares ideal sharp measurements, their probabilities tr(ρP_a), conditional states P_aρP_a/p_a for p_a>0, discarded-outcome states, normalized finite/countable Kraus instruments and abstract trace-class instruments. Apparatus realization remains a separate qualified physical identification.

Assume Countable Choice. For a density operator ρ on a nonzero complex Hilbert space and an orthogonal projection P with p=tr(ρP)>0, ρ_P=PρP/p is a density operator, Pρ_P=ρ_P=ρ_PP, tr(ρ_PP)=1, and orthogonal projections Q with QP=0 have tr(ρ_PQ)=0. For ρ=T(u,u), the update is T(Pu,Pu)/‖Pu‖².

Assume Countable Choice. For a finite/countable orthogonal projection resolution of I and a density operator ρ, Φ(ρ)=Σ_aP_aρP_a converges in trace norm to a density operator, has P_bΦ(ρ)=Φ(ρ)P_b=P_bρP_b, equals Σ_{p_a>0}p_aρ_a, and preserves tr(ρB) for bounded B commuting with every P_a.

Under P1, P2, P3 and Countable Choice, a declared ideal sharp measurement has the stated Born law, repeatable positive-probability conditional branches, the trace-norm discarded ensemble Σ_{p_a>0}p_aρ_a, invariance for commuting bounded quantities, and the stated loss of coherence between distinct outcome ranges.

Under P1, P2, P3 and Countable Choice, a normalized countable family (M_a) with one operator per outcome defines normalized probabilities and a trace-norm discarded ensemble. It is repeatable if and only if M_bM_a=0 for b≠a, equivalently M_a*F_aM_a=F_a for every a. In finite-dimensional H this forces each F_a to be an orthogonal projection; this projection conclusion is not asserted for general H.

On the declared two-level system, the normalized families (P_1,P_2) and (WP_1,P_2) have identical effects but different conditional states after outcome 0. The normalized family (I/√2,B/√2) has effects I/2,I/2 and repeats either outcome with probability 1/2.

concerns.concern: The Statement and F1 call F_a^(1/2) the positive square root supplied by thm-continuous-functional-calculus-for-bounded-self-adjoint-operators. That supplier states an isometric unital star-homomorphism, but does not explicitly state spectral positivity or the positive-square-root corollary. The local argument should identify why the quadratic-form effect inequalities imply σ(F_a)⊆[0,1], then apply the calculus to the square-root function and justify positivity. The dilation algebra is sound once this short corollary is supplied.

Clause (c) asserts that the coherent state differs from the diagonal mixture for every pair of nonzero α,β. Step 2.2 establishes distinguishability explicitly only for α=β=1/√2. For the general assertion, the omitted immediate calculation is ⟨T(ψ,ψ)u,v⟩=conjugate(α)β≠0, whereas the corresponding matrix element of the mixture is zero.

The Sampling remark says that a finite run 'would show frequencies that fluctuate about them under any declared sampling model'. This is too imprecise for the universal sampling qualifier. Identical single-trial marginals do not imply concentration of frequencies: perfectly correlated Bernoulli trials with transmit probability 1/4 have frequency either 0 or 1 for every run length. Specify the sampling assumptions and distinguish expected frequency from concentration or typical finite-run behavior.

alerts.finding: The page's spin-layer paragraph says that the displayed 'standard matrices J_z e_m=me_m and J_± e_m=√((s∓m)(s±m+1)) e_{m±1} ... are self-adjoint'. Its cited prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices clause (a) instead states J_+*=J_-; the self-adjoint operators are J_z,J_x,J_y. For s=1/2, J_+ is the matrix [[0,1],[0,0]], which is not self-adjoint. The page summary misstates its supplier.

Definition (e) displays the local 'conditional updates' as ρ↦(1/p_a)Σ_r(M_{a,r}⊗I)ρ(M_{a,r}⊗I)*, with p_a=tr(ρF_a^loc), without the p_a>0 guard stated by its cited measurement definition (d). Zero-probability outcomes are admissible, so this displayed map needs an explicit domain restriction. The earlier cited definition supplies the intended restriction.

seams_checked.note: Sharp outcome laws and spectral atoms are used with their self-adjointness, domain and choice hypotheses. General instrument updates are explicitly separate from the Born law.

Opened the rank-one, cyclicity, density, Kraus-normalization, finite-effects, abstract-instrument-duality, tensor-map and partial-trace suppliers. Uses retain their mathematical status, boundedness conditions and convergence modes.
States are positive self-adjoint trace-class operators of trace one; pure states are normalized rank-one operators. No state is assigned to a zero vector.

P1, P2, P3 and P7 are read as adopted assumptions and declaration discipline. Repeatability and updates remain conditional model conclusions, with no apparatus realization or empirical result inferred.
Finite preparations are normalized pure states or explicit mixtures. Serial-filter zero-probability branches receive no conditional state.
Rank-one traces and Kraus updates are specialized to C² and C³ with explicit operators. The absorption marker is a declared model level, not an inferred radiation state.
The examples preserve the ideal-filter and apparatus qualifications and report no measured fractions. The separate concern records imprecise sampling prose in the polarizer example.

The Stern-Gerlach example correctly uses the proposition's s=1/2 Pauli matrices and the separate physical spin assignment. The supplier page's erroneous self-adjoint-ladder summary is routed as an alert.

The compatible-joint-law theorem uses finite projection partitions resolving I and applies P3 updates only to positive-probability joint bins. Its repeatability claim remains restricted to the declared ideal instrument.
The error-disturbance remark faithfully separates preparation spread from instrument-dependent state changes and cites equal-effects/different-updates without asserting a universal disturbance bound.

Grouped Kraus normalization, discarded ensembles and ideal local updates are otherwise faithful. The local-instrument definition (e) omits the positive-probability domain restriction on its displayed conditional update; see the routed alert. The no-signalling theorem itself includes p_a>0 and uses normalization rather than the single-Kraus repeatability criterion.

The singlet thought experiment declares a finite tensor-product projection family resolving I and reads its probabilities through the declared ideal measurement law. No laboratory correlation is inferred.
The spin arrangement verifies its four joint projections and uses tr(ρE) as the declared outcome law. Measurement and empirical comparison boundaries remain explicit.

The radiation extension is separately adopted. Ideal analyser and number/window detector models use projection updates, preserve the conditional/discarded distinction and exclude a universal outgoing photon state for absorbers.
The classical/quantized comparison declares two-bin projections and normalizes only nonzero amplitude data. Equal model laws are not presented as empirical proof of quantization.

Spectral-window detection and level-projection probabilities retain the declared measurement reading. Projection norm estimates are used for model probabilities, without converting perturbative coefficients into observed rates or apparatus claims.
